books.section: Topic 6.7 Labor in the Gilded Age

primary_sources: Samuel Gompers, address to the International Labor Congress (August 28, 1893)

options.text: More chances for workers to live fuller, better lives.

options.misconception: Money never appears in the list; Gompers asks for schools, books, and justice.
options.text: More money and nothing else besides money.

options.misconception: Nothing in the passage calls for overthrowing the government.
options.text: The overthrow of the government by force.

options.misconception: Gompers asks for more of many good things, not for an end to business.
options.text: An end to all private business and property.

rationales.A: Gompers ends with more chances to cultivate our better natures, which sums up the whole list.
rationales.B: Money never appears in the list; Gompers asks for schools, books, leisure, and justice.
rationales.C: Nothing in the passage calls for overthrowing the government.
rationales.D: Gompers asks for more of many good things, not for an end to private business.
rationales.general:
Read the list, then read its ending.
1. Gompers asks for more schoolhouses, books, learning, leisure, and justice.
2. None of those is a wage demand.
3. He sums them up as more chances to cultivate our better natures.
4. So the broad want is a fuller, better life, not money alone.
Remember: a list’s closing line often states what the list adds up to.

source: original; stimulus verified against its source (see source_note)
stem: What does Gompers say labor wants most broadly?

stimulus.source_note: Samuel Gompers, address to the International Labor Congress, August 28, 1893. Public domain (Samuel Gompers Papers, University of Maryland).
stimulus.text: “What does labor want? . . . We want more schoolhouses and less jails; more books and less arsenals; more learning and less vice; more constant work and less crime; more leisure and less greed; more justice and less revenge; in fact, more of the opportunities to cultivate our better natures, to make manhood more noble, womanhood more beautiful and childhood more happy and bright.”
